newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks close lower, doubts over Jpn recovery.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks close lower, doubts over Jpn recovery.

text.p: Tokyo stocks closed moderately lower on Wednesday, as sentiment was hurt by doubts over Japan's economic recovery and concerns over the financial health of the nation's firms, brokers said.
These worries prompted active sales, especially in the futures market, they said.
The 225-share Nikkei average lost 156.72 points or 0.79 percent to close at 19,697.17. The index briefly slid as low as 19,495.85.
The Nikkei's September futures dropped 220 points to 19,700.
The Nikkei 225 average closed at the lowest level since May 2, when it finished at 19,514.75.
"The weak sentiment prompted market players to turn their attention to other companies with high credit risks," said Masaaki Higashida, deputy general manager at Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
"But such worries are likely to have a limited impact on the overall market," he said.
On Friday, general contractor Tokai Kogyo Co Ltd decided to apply for court protection from creditors, a move which has weighed on shares in the construction sector.

Behind the overall bearishness were recent economic indicators such as the "tankan" survey which showed a worsening of sentiment among small firms and an improvement among bigger ones, Higashida said.
"The data didn't indicate the Japanese economy could pick up strongly soon," he said.
If the Nikkei 225 average falls from 19,500, the next support level could be 19,000, said Masaki Motohashi, general manger at Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd.
Turnover was 355 million shares on Wednesday, up slightly from 257 million shares traded on Tuesday.
Losers outpaced gainers 755 to 297, while 182 issues were unchanged.
The broader-based TOPIX index fell 5.96 points or 0.40 percent to 1,494.52. The Nikkei 300 average gave up 0.83 point or 0.29 percent to end at 289.67.

Japan's current account surplus in May, widely watched by market participants, was released before the market opened, but a surge in the surplus was within expectations and had only a limited impact on the market, brokers said.
The Finance Ministry said the surplus jumped 154.9 percent to 906.8 billion yen in May, rising for two months in a row.
The surplus in merchandise trade, often a source of bitter rows with United States, surged 118.6 percent in May from a year earlier to 927.9 billion yen, the ministry said.
Shares in supermarket chain operator Yaohan Japan Corp tumbled briefly to an all-time low of 133 yen, dampened by heavy stop-loss sales, although the shares retraced back slightly by close.

Sales were prompted by persistent market jitters over the financial health of the retailer, burdened with hefty borrowings after aggressive expansion overseas. But no major fresh selling factors were detected on Wednesday, traders said.
Yaohan shares ended down 13 yen at 160 yen, making the firm the seventh-largest percentage loser on the first section of the Tokyo bourse. Its volume was the six heaviest at 3.8 million shares.
Financial concerns also depressed contractor Tada Corp, which lost 25 yen or 13.37 percent to end at 162, making it the sharpest percentage loser on the first section.
Banks were also weaker, led by Sakura Bank Ltd, which retreated for the ninth consecutive session, depressed by the dissolving of cross share-holdings, traders said.
Sakura Bank fell 22 yen to 760 in trade totalling 5.8 million shares, making it the third most heavily traded issue.
By sector, decliners were led by fisheries, mining, construction, transportation equipment and warehousing. The major gainers were communications, automobiles, shipbuilding and precision instruments.
The second section index lost 4.60 points to end at 1,801.56, with 7.81 million shares traded.
The over-the-counter (OTC) index was down 4.44 points at 1,187.47.
-- Hiroko Nakata, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-8027
